name: Frame.io
description: Frame.io is Adobe's cloud platform for organizing, reviewing, approving, and delivering video and other creative work. Production teams use it to manage projects and media, collect frame-accurate feedback, share work securely, track metadata, and automate creative workflows.
agentUseSummary: Connect a Frame.io V4 account once through Relay-owned Adobe OAuth, then let agents use every account- and role-authorized API operation under Safe or Dangerous policy.

capabilities.label: Browse creative work
capabilities.description: Read the connected user, accounts, workspaces, projects, folders, files, version stacks, comments, shares, metadata, and search results.

capabilities.label: Manage reviews and media
capabilities.description: Create, update, move, copy, upload, share, comment on, and delete Frame.io resources permitted by the connected user.

capabilities.label: Automate workflows
capabilities.description: Manage webhooks, custom actions, permissions, groups, metadata, collections, and other account-authorized workflow resources.

capabilities.label: Use the complete Frame.io V4 API
capabilities.description: Use every stable current Frame.io V4 operation permitted by the connected account, project roles, plan, and Adobe application.

allowed.label: List accounts
allowed.description: List accounts available to the connected user.

allowed.label: List workspaces
allowed.description: List a bounded page of workspaces in one account.

allowed.label: List projects
allowed.description: List a bounded page of projects in one workspace.

allowed.label: Browse folder
allowed.description: List a bounded page of files, folders, and version stacks in a folder.

allowed.label: List comments
allowed.description: List a bounded page of review comments on one file.

allowed.label: Search creative work
allowed.description: Run a bounded search in one Frame.io account.

approvalRequired.label: Use full Frame.io V4 API
approvalRequired.description: Use any stable current Frame.io V4 operation; Safe mode requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Bounded account, workspace, project, folder, file, comment, and search reads run directly; every other Frame.io operation requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected OAuth- and role-authorized stable Frame.io V4 operation runs without Relay per-action approval; fixed origin, bounds, audits, redaction, ownership, rate limits, and provider enforcement still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts selected Frame.io tools through the authenticated server-side connector.
Railway mounts selected Frame.io tools through the authenticated server-side connector.

providerSetup.blocker: Relay's Adobe Developer Console project, Frame.io V4 API OAuth Web App credential, beta users or production approval, and Railway client credentials are not configured.
providerSetup.nextAction: Sign in to Adobe Developer Console, create a project with the Frame.io V4 API and OAuth Web App credential, register https://api.relayconsole.work/api/v1/marketplace/oauth/frame-io/callback, add beta users and obtain production approval where required, then set FRAME_IO_CLIENT_ID and FRAME_IO_CLIENT_SECRET in Railway.

evidence.supports: Frame.io V4 supports three-legged Adobe IMS user OAuth; Web App credentials are confidential clients and V4 access is authorized by the connected user's Frame.io roles.
Adobe documents authorize/v2, token/v3, confidential-client Basic authentication, offline_access refresh tokens, 24-hour access tokens, 14-day rotating refresh tokens, and the IMS revoke endpoint.

Frame.io documents the V4 resource hierarchy, stable /v4 API origin, cursor pagination, per-operation rate limits, projects, files, folders, comments, shares, search, uploads, metadata, and workflow resources.
The official OpenAPI contract defines the current stable V4 endpoint surface, OAuth scopes, schemas, page-size maximum of 100, and fixed https://api.frame.io server.
Adobe user OAuth credentials begin in development mode with an explicit beta-user allowlist and may require Adobe production approval before any Adobe user can connect.
